subject: Expressing NA's on a correlation matrix plot

messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Expressing NA's on a correlation matrix plot
parts:
Hello ggplotters,

I am attempting to make a correlation matrix plot but I have some NA
values as not all comparisons in the matrix are possible. What I would
like to do is for all values that are NA, the corresponding cell on
the plot is labelled with something that denotes this rather than just
an empty cell.

library(ggplot2)

## Say I have correlation matrix like this one
A <- array(c(0.1, NA, 0.3, NA, 0.4, 0.5, 0.3, NA, 0.4, 0.5), dim=c(4,4))
m <- melt(A)

## Then I plot this like this one.
ggplot(m, aes(X1, X2, fill = value)) +
geom_tile() +
scale_fill_gradient2()

## Any suggestions on how I can express the NA information on a plot like this?

Thanks in advance!

Sam

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Expressing NA's on a correlation matrix plot
parts:
On Saturday, 21 January 2012 at 01:28 , Sam Albers wrote:
> I am attempting to make a correlation matrix plot but I have some NA
> values as not all comparisons in the matrix are possible. What I would
> like to do is for all values that are NA, the corresponding cell on
> the plot is labelled with something that denotes this rather than just
> an empty cell.

## Say I have correlation matrix like this one
A <- array(c(0.1, NA, 0.3, NA, 0.4, 0.5, 0.3, NA, 0.4, 0.5), dim=c(4,4))
m <- melt(A)

# Identify NAs
m$NAlabel <- ifelse(is.na(m$value), "NA", "")

## Then I plot this like this one.
ggplot(m, aes(X1, X2, fill = value)) +
geom_tile() +

scale_fill_gradient2() +
geom_text(aes(label=NAlabel))

# or be more subtle
m$X1NA <- ifelse(is.na(m$value), m$X1, NA)
m$X2NA <- ifelse(is.na(m$value), m$X2, NA)

scale_fill_gradient2() +
geom_point(aes(X1NA, X2NA), size=3, legend=FALSE)
# geom_point(aes(X1NA, X2NA), size=3, show_guide=FALSE) # <- devel
version syntax
# but I am not sure why, without legend=FALSE, points are added to the
legend here: there is nothing to legend. Its probably just difficult
to notice automatically.

# or you could do it like that
m$isNA <- as.numeric(is.na(m$value))

scale_fill_gradient2() +
geom_point(aes(size=isNA), legend=FALSE) +
# draw 0-size points where value is not NA
scale_size(to=c(0,3), legend=FALSE)
# geom_point(aes(size=isNA), show_guide=FALSE) + # <- devel
version syntax
# scale_size(range=c(0,3))
# which suppresses the warning about NA in geom_point

JiHO

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Expressing NA's on a correlation matrix plot
parts:
Actually, my previous suggestions where unnecessarily complex to the
point of being silly. Just subset your data, it'll be much easier:

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape)

## Say I have correlation matrix like this one
A <- array(c(0.1, NA, 0.3, NA, 0.4, 0.5, 0.3, NA, 0.4, 0.5), dim=c(4,4))
m <- melt(A)

ggplot(m, aes(X1, X2, fill = value)) +
geom_tile() +
scale_fill_gradient2() +
geom_text(data=m[is.na(m$value),], label="NA")

ggplot(m, aes(X1, X2)) +
geom_tile(aes(fill = value)) +
scale_fill_gradient2() +
geom_point(data=m[is.na(m$value),])

And you could even do something that usually is a mistake (mapping an
aesthetic to a single value, instead of setting it) to get a legend

ggplot(m, aes(X1, X2)) +
geom_tile(aes(fill = value)) +
scale_fill_gradient2() +
geom_point(aes(size=1), data=m[is.na(m$value),]) +
scale_size(name="", to=c(3,3), breaks=1, label="NA")

but that is really devious.

I think I prefer the most straightforward one (geom_text) but if your
matrix is large then maybe points will turn out to be more elegant.

JiHO
